## Medium Series

<p style="max-width: 650px;">
A four-part series about how business judgment and statistical rigor
combine to make good experimental design — shown here in the order they
were written, since each one builds on the last.
</p>

<div class="writing-entry">
<span class="writing-number">Part 1 of 4</span>
<div class="writing-body">
### Making Data-Driven Decisions: Navigating the Challenges of Business Experiments
<span class="writing-date">AUG 2, 2023</span>

Opens the series by laying out why experimentation matters for
product and strategy decisions, and previews the hard questions —
sample size, duration, and budget and time constraints — that the
rest of the series works through one at a time.

<a class="site-pill" href="https://medium.com/@hjulian_73945/making-data-driven-decisions-navigating-the-challenges-of-business-experiments-84c3306810f4" target="_blank" rel="noopener">

<div class="writing-entry">
<span class="writing-number">Part 2 of 4</span>
<div class="writing-body">
### Experimental Design: Evaluating your Business Risk and its Implications for Design
<span class="writing-date">AUG 17, 2023</span>

Walks through how to weigh the risk of a false positive against the
risk of a false negative, and how that balance should shift depending
on the business context you're actually operating in.

<a class="site-pill" href="https://medium.com/@hjulian_73945/experimental-design-evaluating-your-business-risk-and-its-implications-for-design-4f61de9452cc" target="_blank" rel="noopener">

<span class="writing-number">Part 3 of 4</span>
<div class="writing-body">
### Experimental Design's Ever-Present Gremlin: Statistical Noise
<span class="writing-date">AUG 22, 2023</span>

Digs into why noise is unavoidable in experimental data and what that

<div class="writing-entry">
<span class="writing-number">Part 4 of 4</span>
<div class="writing-body">
### Experimental Design: Zeroing in on your Baseline and Expected Impact
<span class="writing-date">AUG 28, 2023</span>

Closes the series with how to set a defensible expected-impact
estimate for your experiment, and why that number needs to be
grounded in something more than a guess before it drives your
minimum detectable effect.
